sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Portage County, Wisconsin?
sections.html:
The Portage County Treasurer collects and distributes current and delinquent real estate taxes, keeps the primary tax records, and also handles tax foreclosure sales, unclaimed funds and lottery tax credits. The office is at 1516 Church Street, Stevens Point, WI 54481, open Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone number is (715) 346-1348.

Not every Portage County bill goes to the county. The county treasurer collects payments for 23 of the 28 municipalities on the first installment and 27 of 28 on the second. Owners in the City of Stevens Point pay the city for current taxes, and a few towns and one village take the first installment themselves. Read the coupons on your bill to see where your payment goes.

sections.h2: When are Portage County property taxes due, and where do you pay?
sections.html:
Portage County collects taxes in two installments, due January 31 and July 31. Wis. Stat. 74.11 sets the same default for the state, with a first installment on or before January 31 and a second on or before July 31, and requires full payment by January 31 when the parcel's total tax is under $100. The county sends one bill a year with two stubs and no reminder notices.

Where the parcel isWho gets the paymentInstallments
City of Stevens PointCity of Stevens Point treasurerThree: January 31, April 30, July 31
Towns of Almond, Belmont, Lanark and Village of MilladoreThe municipal treasurer for the first installmentCounty takes the second
Towns of Alban, Amherst, Buena Vista, Carson, Dewey, Grant, Hull, Linwood, New Hope, Pine Grove, Plover, Sharon, StocktonPortage County TreasurerAll installments
Villages of Almond, Amherst, Amherst Junction, Junction City, Nelsonville, Park Ridge, Plover, Rosholt, WhitingPortage County TreasurerAll installments

The county treasurer's page lists these municipalities as the ones where the county collects all installments. Delinquent City of Stevens Point taxes are collected by Portage County.

sections.h2: How do you pay the Portage County treasurer, and what are the fees?
sections.html:
You can pay by mail, at the office window, at a partner bank, online or by phone. Checks and cash at the office window or in the mail carry no fee. The county's online system is at landinfo.co.portage.wi.gov, and its vendor, Point and Pay, charges fees that the taxpayer pays.

  • Credit card: 2.39 percent of the payment, or the same rate if called in.
  • Visa debit card: $3.95 online or 2.39 percent by phone. Other debit cards are charged as credit cards.
  • Electronic check: $1.50.
  • Phone line: 1-877-782-4828, an automated line that asks for the tax year and your bill number.
  • Partner banks: Community First Bank in Rosholt, International Bank of Amherst, and Pineries Bank in Stevens Point.

When you search for a parcel online, the county says to use only the parcel number, formatted as on the bill. Mail payments to Portage County Treasurer, 1516 Church Street, Stevens Point, WI 54481. The office is closed November 26 and 27 and December 24 and 25, 2026.

sections.h2: What happens if a Portage County tax payment is late?
sections.html:
Taxes become delinquent on the sixth business day after the due date, because of the five working day grace period. The second installment option is lost if a date is missed, and the entire bill becomes due. Interest begins at 1.5 percent per month on the unpaid balance in the month after the due date, so a missed first installment shows 1.5 percent the day after the grace period and 3 percent in March, according to the county. The county treasurer adds that other fees may apply and asks you to call for a final payoff figure.

State law sets the base rate. Wis. Stat. 74.47 sets interest on delinquent taxes at one percent per month or fraction of a month and lets a county board add a penalty of up to 0.5 percent per month by ordinance. Portage County's published rate of 1.5 percent is consistent with that combination.

  • If property taxes remain unpaid on September 1, a tax certificate is issued and a Notice of Issuance of Tax Certificate goes to the owner.
  • The owner then has two years to pay the balance for that tax year.
  • If the taxes are not paid by the end of the two years, the county forecloses through the tax deed process.
  • The county does not offer payment plans on delinquent taxes, but it accepts payments of any amount at any time.

The Foundation for Rural Housing, working through the State of Wisconsin, offers funds for several situations including delinquent taxes. Its numbers are 608-238-3448 and 888-400-5974.

sections.h2: How does Stevens Point collect property taxes?
sections.html:
The City of Stevens Point collects all three installments of current taxes at its own treasurer's office, 1515 Strongs Avenue, Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The three coupons at the bottom of the bill are due January 31, April 30 and July 31. If you miss any payment, the whole unpaid balance goes delinquent and interest of one percent per month is charged from February 1. The city notes that Portage County adds penalties if taxes remain delinquent after July 31.

The city's online lookup shows tax bills, due dates and payoff for a future date, and online fees are $1.50 for e-check, 1.5 percent for debit with a $2.00 minimum, and 2.40 percent for credit with a $2.00 minimum. Delinquent taxes for earlier years are handled by the county treasurer at 715-346-1348. A star in the box under the parcel number on a Stevens Point bill marks a prior year delinquency.

sections.h2: What credits can lower a Portage County tax bill?
sections.html:
Portage County lists three credits on its treasurer's page:

  • The school levy tax credit is applied automatically to every bill.
  • The first dollar credit is applied automatically to a parcel that has an improvement.
  • The lottery and gaming credit is for your primary residence. It must be claimed, and you can claim it on only one parcel.

The state's rules say you must be a Wisconsin resident who owns a dwelling and lives in it as your primary residence as of January 1. Rentals, business property, vacant land and garages do not qualify. Apply to the treasurer by January 31 after you receive the bill, or file a late claim with the Department of Revenue by October 1. The treasurer's page also posts yearly mill rate sheets for 2021 through 2025.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a property assessment in Portage County?
sections.html:
Your appeal begins with the assessor and the board of review for the city, town or village where the house sits. Ask that municipal clerk for the assessor's contact details and the board of review dates. Under Wis. Stat. 70.47, you must give the board clerk notice of intent to object at least 48 hours before the first meeting and file a written objection within the first two hours of that meeting, unless the board waives the notice for good cause.

Portage County's assessors are listed by town, village and city, so the municipal clerk is the right first call.

sections.h2: What should you know when selling a house in Portage County?
sections.html:
Confirm which office holds your bill, then ask that treasurer for a payoff figure before you set a closing date. A sale in Stevens Point involves the city for current taxes and the county for delinquent ones. A sale elsewhere in the county usually involves the county treasurer for the second installment.

  • A completed electronic real estate transfer return is required for every conveyance of an ownership interest, and you prepare it on the Department of Revenue website.
  • Property Fraud Alert, offered through the county's recorder, tracks recordings that affect your name.
  • Land records can be searched online through the county's Tapestry site, and the Wisconsin Real Estate Sales Finder shows sales data.
  • Ask your closing agent how the year's tax is divided between you and the buyer under your contract.

sections.h2: What is Portage County like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Stevens Point is the seat of Portage County. It was created from the Wisconsin Territory in 1836 and organized in 1844, and takes its name from the portage between the Fox and Wisconsin rivers. The county covers 823 square miles, of which 801 are land, and the 2020 census found 63.4 percent of residents in urban areas.

The Census Bureau estimated the population at 71,943 on July 1, 2025, a 2.2 percent increase from 2020. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied rate was 69.7 percent, the median value of owner-occupied homes was $243,100, and median gross rent was $940. There were 29,679 households and 32,398 housing units, with 244 building permits in 2025. Median household income was $76,070 and 20.8 percent of residents were 65 or older.

faqs.q: When are Portage County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due in two installments, January 31 and July 31. The City of Stevens Point collects three installments, due January 31, April 30 and July 31. The county sends no reminder notices, so mark the dates.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Portage County?
faqs.a: Pay the county treasurer at 1516 Church Street, Stevens Point, unless your parcel is in the City of Stevens Point, the Towns of Almond, Belmont or Lanark, or the Village of Milladore. Those pay their own treasurer for the first installment, and Stevens Point for all current installments.

faqs.q: What interest does Portage County charge on delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: The county states 1.5 percent per month on the unpaid balance, starting the month after the due date. State law sets interest at one percent per month and allows a county penalty of up to 0.5 percent. Call (715) 346-1348 for a payoff.

faqs.q: How long before Portage County forecloses for unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: A tax certificate is issued if taxes are unpaid on September 1, and the owner has two years to pay that year's balance. If it stays unpaid after two years, the county forecloses using the tax deed process.

faqs.q: Does Portage County offer payment plans for late property taxes?
faqs.a: No. The treasurer states it does not offer payment plans on delinquent taxes, but accepts payments of any amount at any time. The Foundation for Rural Housing offers funds for some delinquent tax situations at 608-238-3448.
